the_distinction_this_report_keeps: an EVIDENCE GAP is not a DEFECT. A breach of a working rule - a banned directory listing, a stray file in a shared directory - is a process failure that often leaves no mark on the corpus. A MATERIAL DEFECT is something wrong in what ships. Both are reported and they are never added into one number, because a combined count tells the owner nothing about risk.

Counts are from SP/campaign/transcript_coverage_census.v1.json (observed: 6 of 57 in Lam, 5 of 74 in Jer). The earlier wording said "the 43 Lamentations attempts and all Jeremiah attempts"; 43 was a transcript-mapping count used as if it were an attempt count, and "all Jeremiah attempts" was wrong because five were observed.

what_this_report_does_not_claim: It does not claim the campaign has no undiscovered breaches. It reports what was DISCOVERED, and the discovery method for most of it - reading runtime transcripts - reached only a small fraction of attempts. The coverage is stated as a per-book census, not as a remembered ratio: Transcript-based observation covered 11 attempts in total: 5 in Jer (6.8% of its 74 attempts), 6 in Lam (10.5% of its 57 attempts). Every other book, including every other book before Jeremiah, had zero observed attempts. The honest statement is that the breach rate among OBSERVED attempts was high and that most attempts were never observable. Coverage numbers come from SP/campaign/transcript_coverage_census.v1.json, which is rebuilt from the receipts, manifests and stage-1 audit packets; they are not restated from prose here.
authority: orchestrator report ordered by OW-8; candidate-only, non-authorizing

transcript_coverage_census.note: observed = a stage-1 auditor read the transcript and wrote per-transcript findings. It is the only number that supports a claim about discovered breaches, and it is counted, never estimated.

superseded_statements.text: It does not claim the campaign has no undiscovered breaches. It reports what was DISCOVERED, and the discovery method for most of it - reading runtime transcripts - existed for about one attempt in eight in Lamentations and for none of the earlier books. The honest statement is that the breach rate among OBSERVED attempts was high and that most attempts were never observable.
superseded_statements.why_superseded: It said the transcript-reading method existed "for none of the earlier books". Jeremiah is an earlier book and five of its attempts were observed and are cited by name in this same report. The Lamentations figure ("about one attempt in eight") was also a remembered ratio; the counted figure is 6 of 57.
superseded_statements.retained_because: this campaign does not rewrite history; a corrected claim is kept beside its correction
